notes: Tests genuinely exercise the change: web/test/csvExport.test.mjs passes (node --test); Go unit test covers csvCell; the integration test TestTheExportedCSVCannotCarryAFormula was run against a throwaway Postgres 16 and passes on HEAD, and fails (two assertions) when the single `record[i] = csvCell(record[i])` line in analytics.go:1001 is removed — so it does verify the fix, not just the helper.
go vet ./internal/httpapi clean; the rest of the httpapi integration suite still passes with the change.
Only two CSV producers exist in the repo (exportEvents CSV branch and DataTable download) and both are covered; the NDJSON branch is untouched, which is correct.

Minor inconsistency, not a defect: Go csvCell prefixes any stringified value (a negative number would become '-3) while the TS csvValue only prefixes typeof string values. No exported Go column carries a negative number today (contract_version is positive, timestamp starts with a digit), so behaviour matches the commit message in practice.

Behavioural change for programmatic consumers of the CSV export: any string cell beginning with = + - @ now carries a leading apostrophe (e.g. a campaign named '-' or a user_id starting with '-'). Modern Excel shows the apostrophe literally on CSV import rather than swallowing it. This is the OWASP-recommended mitigation and is fully reverted by reverting the commit; no migration or persisted state involved.

DataTable.tsx change is a straight extraction of searchableValue/csvValue into csvExport.ts (cellText keeps identical semantics for the search filter) — in scope, since it exists to make the rule unit-testable.
